question.text: Two capacitors with capacitance values <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>2000</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi>pF</mi></math>  and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>3000</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi>pF</mi></math> are connected in series. The voltage applied across this combination is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>00</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>02</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The percentage error in the calculation of the energy stored in this combination of capacitors is __________.

solution.text:
For the purpose of calculation of error, fundamental formula is considered

1C=1C1+1C2⇒C=1200 pF

-dCC12=-dC1C12-dC2C22

dC=6 pF

Equivalent capacitance =1200±6 pF

E=1/2 CV2

(dE/E=dC/C+2dV/V)×100

=1.3%
